consent.title: MOMentum: A Digital Women's Health Intervention Targeting Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM)
consent.subtitle: Participation Information and Consent Form
consent.intro: We appreciate your decision to participate in this project. Please read the text below carefully and check the box if you agree with the study conditions. We are happy to answer questions or provide additional information if required.
consent.purpose: This survey aims to conduct a test for the MOMentum App prototype. By interacting with the demo, participants will help evaluate the tool's functional design and its effectiveness in supporting GDM management. Your insights will be crucial in refining the digital intervention before its final development.
consent.whoTitle: Who can participate in the study?
consent.who: Anyone older than 18 years old, having experience with GDM.
consent.procedure1: Participation in this study involves completing an online questionnaire, which will take approximately 5–10 minutes. The questionnaire covers topics related to epidemiologic information, the experience with GDM and digital health technologies. There are no right or wrong answers — we are simply interested in your personal views and experiences.
consent.procedure2: Participation is voluntary. You may withdraw from the study at any time without providing a reason and without facing any disadvantages.
consent.procedure3: Your responses will be strictly confidential. All data will be anonymized and stored in a way that prevents any identification of individual participants.
consent.procedure4: Anonymized aggregated data might be published in scientific outlets.
consent.procedure5: Should you choose to withdraw your data after participation, you may do so at any point until July 30, 2026. After this date, all data will have been fully anonymized and can no longer be linked to individual participants.
consent.risks: There are no known risks associated with this study. If you feel uncomfortable at any point, you may stop the interview or questionnaire at any time. Your participation will contribute to the development of better data for female health research.
consent.question: Do you agree to the above consent form?

do.1: Do a few light pregnancy-safe stretches.
do.2: Change positions and avoid sitting too long.
do.3: Roll your shoulders and relax your neck.
do.4: Do a quick posture check and sit with support.
do.5: Walk around the room for 2–3 minutes.
do.6: Step outside for a little fresh air.
do.7: Do a few pelvic floor squeezes.
do.8: Move your ankles and feet to ease stiffness.
do.9: Take a short, slow walk after a meal if you feel comfortable.

eat.2: Have a small healthy snack instead of skipping food.
eat.3: Eat a fruit with a protein or fat pairing, like apple with nut butter.
eat.4: Have yogurt or another simple calcium-rich snack.
eat.5: Add a vegetable to your next meal.
eat.6: Choose a protein-rich bite, like eggs, yogurt, cheese, beans, or nuts.
eat.7: Sip water slowly if you have been forgetting to drink.
eat.8: Have a light snack if nausea feels better when you avoid an empty stomach.
eat.9: Make a simple nourishing drink, like milk or a smoothie if tolerated.

relax.1: Close your eyes and rest for 1 minute.
relax.2: Unclench your jaw and drop your shoulders.
relax.3: Put your phone away for 5 minutes.
relax.4: Sit quietly and breathe into your belly and ribs gently.
relax.6: Rest your legs and feet for a few minutes.
relax.7: Say one kind thing to yourself and your body.
relax.8: Do a short gratitude pause for yourself and baby.
relax.9: Lie or sit comfortably and do a 2-minute calm breathing reset.
